solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In the past, clothing round a pub frightened person when out?

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

indicators.note: the garment wraps round the next pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a robe is a garment, an item of clothing
PH is the map abbreviation for a public house

explanation.surface: Someone from long ago, wearing a robe and making for a pub, is scared of being out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sits after the garment, so the robe goes round A + PH; 'clothing' is the robe itself, not the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An agoraphobic fears open or public spaces, so being outdoors frightens them.

clue.text: Assistant's throwaway comment releasing little special

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of a letter from the word before

parts.note: an aside is a remark made in passing
S is the short form of special

explanation.surface: An assistant mutters a throwaway remark that lets slip something minor but special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' drops S from ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Way to climb height, producing exasperated comment

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Tao is the Way in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A mountain path up a height draws a cross remark from a walker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to climb' reads upwards, so the Way is spelt bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word blurted out in irritation, a curse.

clue.text: Trouble of the last toe?

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a pain in the smallest toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' looks like the definition's noun, but it also stirs up OF THE LAST TOE; the whole clue then describes the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal infection usually starts in the skin between the outermost toes, a common trouble there.

clue.text: Rugby post arrangement curtailed crowd

parts.note: rugby goalposts form the shape of the letter H

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: an order is an arrangement or sequence

explanation.surface: A rugby goalpost set-up, cut short, is overrun by a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng of people.

clue.text: Part of car tilted going through Birmingham

indicators.note: going through means one piece passes into the middle of the other

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for the English city of Birmingham
raked means sloped or tilted, as a stage is

explanation.surface: A car leaning over as it drives through Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the everyday nickname for Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake drum is the rotating cylinder of a drum brake, a component of a vehicle's wheel.

clue.text: Crash, parking in motorway access road

parts.note: to ram is to crash into something
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A collision while parking on a slip road onto the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slip road joining or leaving a motorway, as in an on-ramp.

clue.text: Shortened song penned by a US writer is the last item

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its end

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song

explanation.surface: A truncated song written by an American author closes the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' drops the song's last letter; 'penned by' means held inside the A and the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse, or Book of Revelation, is the final book of the Bible, its closing item.

clue.text: Drug proved fake, after lecturer injected, like some sort of pig?

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: injected means put inside, apt beside a drug

parts.note: belied means showed to be false

explanation.surface: A drug shown to be bogus once a teacher had injected it, as though testing on a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' puts L into BELIED to give BELLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vietnamese pot-bellied pig is a breed named for its rounded paunch.

clue.text: Wife's warning to ditch husband, doing things individually?

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

indicators.note: to ditch means to drop the letter that follows

parts.note: a threat is a warning of harm

explanation.surface: A wife threatening to leave her husband so each can go their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ditch' removes H from THREAT, giving TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch treat is an outing where each person pays their own share, so costs are borne individually.

clue.text: President, not elected, shows disappointed face

parts.note: a candidate who is not elected is out of office

explanation.surface: A president who lost the vote shows a sulky expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A pout is a pushing out of the lips that shows sulkiness or displeasure.

clue.text: Pointed item wrecked the toilets and most of tree

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are smashed into a new order
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone trashed the toilets and nearly all of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges THE TOILETS into STILETTOHE; 'most of' cuts ELM to EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto heel is a tall, thin, tapering shoe heel, sharp as a dagger.

clue.text: Break window with people? Make excuse mostly with a street getting spoiled

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: to defend an action is to make an excuse for it

indicators.note: getting spoiled means the words are ruined and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Smashing a window with a crowd, then offering lame excuses as the street is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DEFEND to DEFEN; 'getting spoiled' turns A STREET into ESTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To defenestrate is to throw someone out of a window, which a playful reading calls breaking it with people.

clue.text: Father hears unhappily about crime, put in other words

indicators.note: about means the earlier pieces go round the next one

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: unhappily means the letters are in a disturbed state, so rearranged

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: A father is upset to hear about an offence, so he restates it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' scrambles only 'hears'; the crime then lands at the join between father and the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate something using different wording.

clue.text: Consequence of smoking after turning in in sitcom, possibly

indicators.note: turning means the little word is spun round
possibly means these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A sitcom character's cigarette habit leads to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes IN into NI; 'possibly' rearranges IN SITCOM into COTINISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotinism is poisoning by nicotine, a result of heavy tobacco use.

clue.text: Unreliable friend in affair around start of last month

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: an amour is a love affair
the first of December, the year's last month, can be written I DEC

explanation.surface: A false friend involved in a fling that began early last month.
explanation.walkthrough: I DEC is 1 December, the start of the last month, with I as the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase, literally a courtier's friend, means a fair-weather friend who cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Unopened file about male expert

indicators.note: about means wrapping round the next piece
unopened means without its first letter

parts.note: a folder is a file for papers
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: An unopened file about a man is handed to a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' takes the first letter off the file before it goes 'about' the male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone very experienced at something.

clue.text: Line of Kings not initially describing how they want their subjects to be?

definitions.text: describing how they want their subjects to be?

indicators.note: not initially means losing the first letter

parts.note: royal means of or belonging to kings

explanation.surface: A dynasty describing what kings hope their people will be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Kings' is the adjective for royalty; 'not initially' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs wish their subjects to be faithful, devoted to the crown.

clue.text: Showing detached attitude? One's upped the dope

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'

indicators.note: upped means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a dope is a fool, a stupid person

explanation.surface: Someone outsmarts an idiot while staying coolly indifferent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' turns FOOL into LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and reserved, standing apart from others.

clue.text: Missed tea badly — here's coffee?

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together poorly, so jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sorely missed their tea but is offered coffee instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup in which strong black coffee is served.

clue.text: Rover's Return? Here's a consequence or two!

definitions.text: Rover's Return? Here's a consequence or two!

parts.words: Rover's Return? Here's a consequence or two!
parts.note: a drink of more alcohol to cure a hangover, a dog's coat coming back, following a drink or two

explanation.surface: A nod to the Rovers Return, the pub in the British TV soap Coronation Street, and the drinks it serves.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock dog's name; the phrase is a morning drink taken after 'one or two' the night before.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a hangover cure, more of what caused it, literally a part of a dog.

clue.text: Bird cry at Loch Ness sees English pushing forward

indicators.note: pushing forward means the letter is moved to the front

parts.note: greet is Scots for weep or cry

explanation.surface: A bird calls by Loch Ness as an Englishman shoves ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of GREET moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron with white plumage.

clue.text: Narrow view overlooks front of this travel document

indicators.note: overlooks means leaves out what follows

parts.note: a vista is a view seen through a narrow opening, as between trees

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone with a narrow outlook ignores the front page of their passport document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' removes T, the front of 'this', from VISTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an endorsement allowing entry to a country, needed for travel.

clue.text: Comfortably avoiding opening tin that's not tasty?

indicators.note: avoiding opening means the word's start is skipped

parts.note: snugly means comfortably and cosily
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Someone sits cosily without opening a tin of food that's unappetising.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasty here is the sense of tasteful, so its opposite is unsightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unpleasant to look at, lacking in good taste.

clue.text: Vehicles heading off where wheel turns?

indicators.note: heading off means removing the first letter

parts.note: taxis are vehicles for hire

explanation.surface: Cabs set off, wheels turning.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line or pin around which a wheel rotates.

clue.text: Silver: consequence of loss is distressing

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
grieving is the mourning that follows a bereavement

explanation.surface: Losing the family silver brings sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrieving means causing distress or a sense of injury.

clue.text: Award or prize Judge dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so dropped from the word

parts.note: to prize open, prise in British spelling, is to jemmy something with a lever

explanation.surface: A prize is handed out once the judge has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is the verb to force open, not a noun beside 'Award'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is an American television award.

clue.text: Butterfly frightened mountaineer who's removed cap

parts.note: frit is British dialect for frightened

indicators.note: removed cap means the top letter is taken off

parts.note: Sir Edmund Hillary, with Tenzing Norgay, first climbed Everest

explanation.surface: A scared climber takes off a cap on seeing a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIT is northern English dialect for scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritillaries are a group of butterflies with chequered orange-and-black wings.
